title: Having Understanding
note: This means having your own true understanding, alongside what comes from learning and listening.

couplets.plain: Understanding is a tool that guards against ruin, and a fort inside that even enemies can’t destroy.
couplets.pm: For rulers, understanding is the tool that keeps ruin from coming: to guard is to see ahead and prevent it. More than that, it is an inner fort that enemies can’t destroy. It can also mean a fort they can’t enter and destroy.

links.quote: a fort inside that even enemies can’t destroy
links.reason: Gives understanding as a tool against ruin and a fort that no enemy can destroy.

couplets.plain: Understanding doesn’t let the mind go wherever it goes. It turns it from evil and guides it to good.
couplets.pm: Understanding doesn’t let the mind go to whichever sense it has gone to. It weighs the good and bad there, draws the mind off the bad and drives it to the good. There are five senses, but the mind goes to one at a time. As a groom knows the ground and steers a horse, understanding knows the sense and steers the mind.
couplets.note: The Tamil doesn’t name what is steered. He supplies the mind, and the plain reading follows him.

links.quote: It turns it from evil and guides it to good
links.reason: Says what understanding does: it reins in the mind and turns it to the good.

couplets.plain: Whatever you hear, from whoever’s mouth, understanding is seeing the reality in it.
couplets.pm: Whatever is said, by whoever says it, understanding can see its true worth. All people shift between the three qualities, so high things may come from low mouths, low things from the high, good counsel from enemies and ruin from friends. So take or leave a thing by its worth, not by the nature of the speaker.

links.quote: Whatever you hear, from whoever’s mouth

couplets.plain: Understanding is saying things so that they go home and are easy to grasp, and seeing the subtle meaning in what others say.
couplets.pm: Understanding can say hard things so that they come easily to the listener, and can see the fine meaning in the words of others, however hard that is. Say what you say clearly and without fault. What you hear may be faulty and unclear, but take what is useful in it.

links.quote: seeing the subtle meaning in what others say

couplets.plain: To embrace the world is cleverness. Not to bloom and then close is understanding.
couplets.pm: Making the world your friend is brightness, and staying constant in that friendship, not blooming at first and closing later, is understanding. The world here means the great. Be their friend unchanging, like a flower on a tree and not one on a pond, and you gain every joy. Some read it as not blooming in wealth and not closing in poverty.

links.quote: Not to bloom and then close is understanding
links.reason: Gives understanding an even temper that neither blooms nor closes.

couplets.plain: However the world lives, understanding is living that way with the world.
couplets.pm: Whichever way the world goes, it is a ruler’s understanding to go that way with it. A ruler who thinks “I rule the world and no one rules me” and acts as he pleases earns sin and blame, and that isn’t understanding.

links.quote: understanding is living that way with the world
links.reason: Counts moving in step with the world as part of understanding itself.

couplets.plain: Those with understanding know what will be. Those without it can’t know that.
couplets.pm: Those with understanding can know in advance what is to come, by thinking ahead. Those without it can’t know until it has arrived. Some read “what will be” as what is good for them.

links.reason: Sets those who know what will be against those who can’t.

couplets.plain: Not to fear what should be feared is folly. To fear what should be feared is the way of those who understand.
couplets.pm: Not fearing what should be feared, such as sin, blame and ruin, is folly: acting without thought. Fearing it, thinking and holding back, is the work of those with understanding. Don’t scorn it as weakness. Fearlessness was praised in a ruler, and this shows where fear is needed.

links.quote: To fear what should be feared is the way of those who understand
links.reason: Praises the fear that stops you before the danger, not after.

links.quote: Not to fear what should be feared is folly
links.reason: Puts not fearing what should be feared down as plain folly.

couplets.plain: Those with the understanding to guard against what is to come have no suffering that comes and shakes them.
couplets.pm: Those with the understanding to foresee what is coming and guard against it have no suffering that comes to make them tremble. Guarding means removing its cause.

links.quote: guard against what is to come
links.reason: Promises those who guard against what is to come that no suffering will shake them.

couplets.plain: Those with understanding have everything. Those without it, whatever they have, have nothing.
couplets.pm: Those with understanding have everything, even if they have nothing else. Those without it have nothing, even if they have everything. All things are made and guarded by understanding. Without it you have no means to keep what you have, or to make it again when god brings ruin.

ideaLinks.quote: doesn’t let the mind go wherever it goes
ideaLinks.reason: Understanding is what keeps the mind from going wherever it goes.
